dish:Xuixo.name: Xuixo
dish:Xuixo.hook: Girona's fried cream horn — a real pastry with a documented address, not a folk tale.
dish:Xuixo.text: Created in the 1920s (family accounts say from about 1918) by the confectioner Emili Puig on Carrer de la Cort Reial, reputedly after a French pastry worker showed him a cream-filled technique. Technique: a yeasted, laminated dough is shaped into a cylinder, deep-fried, then filled with crema catalana and rolled in granulated sugar while still warm so the sugar catches. Eat it hot; the sugar has to crackle. A carnival legend of the acrobat 'el Tarlà' sneezing 'xui-xui' runs alongside the Puig story — that part is folklore. The pastry carries the Catalan 'Producte de la Terra' mark, and the 'best in Girona' title is a live rivalry, not a settled fact.

dish:Mar i muntanya.name: Mar i muntanya
dish:Mar i muntanya.hook: Sea-and-mountain in one pot — pollastre amb escamarlans, chicken with langoustines, the Empordà's signature paradox.
dish:Mar i muntanya.text: Born of fishing-family economy — chicken as the cheap protein, shellfish to stretch the pot. Technique: a slow sofregit base, then a picada stirred in at the very end — coarse salt, fried bread, almonds, hazelnuts, garlic, parsley, sometimes the fried chicken liver or a square of dark chocolate — to thicken and perfume the sauce. The picada is the whole trick; add it too early and it splits. A festive main across the Empordà and Costa Brava.

dish:Suquet de peix.name: Suquet de peix
dish:Suquet de peix.hook: The fishermen's stew, thickened by potato starch and an almond picada — never flour.
dish:Suquet de peix.text: Cooked originally aboard from unsellable catch (rockfish classically, then monkfish or hake); the name comes from 'suquejar', to release juice. Technique: fish and potatoes simmered in a garlic-tomato sofregit, finished with a picada of toasted bread, garlic, parsley and almonds — the almond picada plus the potato starch is the textural signature. Roses is the reference port; eat it in the harbour towns.

dish:Niu de Palafrugell.name: Niu de Palafrugell
dish:Niu de Palafrugell.hook: A baroque winter stew of cod tripe and stockfish that only surfaces for a few weeks a year.
dish:Niu de Palafrugell.text: A Palafrugell-specific dish, originally a meatless Lenten pot of cod tripe, peixopalo (dried stockfish), potato and egg; cork-factory workers later enriched it with game birds and sausage, fishermen with cuttlefish. Technique: about five hours total — roughly an hour on the sofregit, four hours slow — finished with allioli. Today it appears only during the organised 'Es Niu' campaign each winter (Jan–Feb) at a handful of Palafrugell tables.

dish:Canelons de Sant Esteve.name: Canelons de Sant Esteve
dish:Canelons de Sant Esteve.hook: The 26 December cannelloni built from Christmas Day's leftover meat.
dish:Canelons de Sant Esteve.text: Canelons reached Catalonia through Italian cooks in late-18th-century Barcelona fondes; the Sant Esteve tradition is a 20th-century habit, not medieval. Technique: pasta sheets rolled around the shredded beef, chicken and pork left over from Christmas Day's escudella / carn d'olla, layered under béchamel and grated cheese and gratinéed. Eaten on 26 December, Catalonia's second Christmas Day, at the family table.

dish:Botifarra amb fesols de Santa Pau.name: Botifarra amb fesols de Santa Pau
dish:Botifarra amb fesols de Santa Pau.hook: Grilled pork sausage with the small beans grown on Garrotxa volcanic soil — a DOP since 2015.
dish:Botifarra amb fesols de Santa Pau.text: The sausage-and-beans pairing first appears in print in the 1830 cookbook 'Nou manual per cuinar amb tota la perfecció'; in Girona province the defining beans are the Fesols de Santa Pau (Tavella Brisa, Setsetmanera and Gra Petit varieties), grown on the volcanic soils of the Garrotxa and PDO-protected since 2015. Technique: a raw pork botifarra grilled over coals, the beans slow-simmered until they turn creamy, dressed with the sausage fat. Best in Garrotxa village kitchens.

dish:Anxova de l'Escala.name: Anxova de l'Escala
dish:Anxova de l'Escala.hook: Hand-salted anchovies barrel-cured up to a year, from a single fishing town down the coast.
dish:Anxova de l'Escala.text: L'Escala's curing houses go back to firms like Solés (1888) and Callol Serrats. Technique: fresh anchovies are hand-gutted, layered in salt in wooden barrels, pressed and left to mature 10–12 months at ambient temperature — the wood barrel, not plastic, is held essential to a correct cure. Eaten as a tapa on bread with oil; sold straight from the L'Escala factories. Strong local identity, but note: it carries no EU protection — a regional 'Producte de la Terra', not an IGP.

dish:Gamba de Palamós.name: Gamba de Palamós
dish:Gamba de Palamós.hook: The red prawn sold live off the boat at auction, under its own guarantee mark.
dish:Gamba de Palamós.text: Aristeus antennatus, landed by a specialised trawler fleet and auctioned twice daily at the Confraria de Pescadors de Palamós; the 'Marca de Garantia Gamba de Palamós' checks fishing ground, texture, count-per-kilo and landing temperature before any lot may carry the name. Technique: eat it barely seared a la planxa — seconds a side — to keep the creamy head juices; overcooking it is the local sin. A guarantee mark, not an EU PDO — don't conflate the two. Prices run high and volatile in season.

walks:Passeig de la Muralla.name: Passeig de la Muralla
walks:Passeig de la Muralla.hook: The wall-top walk on a Carolingian circuit over Roman foundations.
walks:Passeig de la Muralla.text: One of the longest early-medieval wall circuits in Europe, 9th–10th c., rebuilt over 1st-c. BCE Roman lines because Girona sat on the Carolingian–al-Andalus frontier. Free; open 8:00–21:00 (to 23:00 Jun–Aug). The towers give the best rooftop views of the Cathedral and the plain.

walks:The Onyar bridges.name: The Onyar bridges
walks:The Onyar bridges.hook: Seven bridges, one row of reflected houses.
walks:The Onyar bridges.text: Walk bank to bank across the Onyar's footbridges — the Eiffel-company Pont de les Peixateries Velles (1877) is the one to stand on — watching the cases de l'Onyar double themselves in the water. The colours were fixed by a 1980s restoration led by the painter Enric Ansesa and architects, not chosen at random.

walks:The Call labyrinth.name: The Call labyrinth
walks:The Call labyrinth.hook: The steep black-stone lanes of the medieval Jewish quarter.
walks:The Call labyrinth.text: Off Carrer de la Força, the Call folds into stepped alleys, cisterns and dead-ends — one of Europe's best-preserved Jewish quarters. End at the Museu d'Història dels Jueus in the Centre Bonastruc ça Porta. Wear grippy soles; the stone polishes to glass in the rain.

walks:Vall de Sant Daniel.name: Vall de Sant Daniel
walks:Vall de Sant Daniel.hook: A green valley of springs and plane trees ten minutes past the walls.
walks:Vall de Sant Daniel.text: Behind Montjuïc the city stops and a wooded valley of natural springs (the Font del Ferro among them) runs up to the Romanesque monastery of Sant Daniel. A cool, shaded escape in August and the quiet counterweight to the Barri Vell.

walks:Parc de la Devesa.name: Parc de la Devesa
walks:Parc de la Devesa.hook: The largest urban park in Catalonia, under 2,500 plane trees.
walks:Parc de la Devesa.text: On the Mercadal side, a grid of plane trees planted in the 19th century throws deep shade over gravel avenues; it doubles as the fairground for the Fires de Sant Narcís each autumn. Bring a book and disappear.

walks:Castell de Sant Miquel.name: Castell de Sant Miquel
walks:Castell de Sant Miquel.hook: A hill climb to the ruined castle above the city, for the whole valley.
chips: Early, for the haze to lift
walks:Castell de Sant Miquel.text: A signed path leaves the Vall de Sant Daniel and climbs through holm oak to the ruined Castell de Sant Miquel (~380 m), with the four-river plain, the Pyrenees to the north and, on a clear day, a glint of the Costa Brava. Take water.

walks:The Cathedral-to-Sant Feliu spine.name: The Cathedral-to-Sant Feliu spine
walks:The Cathedral-to-Sant Feliu spine.hook: The stone heart, from the widest nave to the eight Roman tombs.
walks:The Cathedral-to-Sant Feliu spine.text: From the Cathedral's Baroque staircase down Pujada de Sant Domènec to the Basílica de Sant Feliu, where eight 3rd–4th-c. Roman and early-Christian sarcophagi are set into the presbytery walls — the densest run of history in the city, walkable before breakfast.

coffee-gardens:Palau Fugit — Gipsy bar &.name: Palau Fugit — Gipsy bar & El Terrat
coffee-gardens:Palau Fugit — Gipsy bar &.hook: Barri Vell (Carrer Bonaventura Carreras i Peralta, 4)
coffee-gardens:Palau Fugit — Gipsy bar &.text: El Equipo Creativo (interiors) with Isern Associats (architecture) resurrected the long-abandoned 18th-century Baroque palace Casa Heras de Puig as a 24-room hotel in 2023: a custom Yves Klein-blue reception table under a golden chandelier against original stone, a palette lifted from the Onyar riverside façades and the Temps de Flors festival, custom nanimarquina rugs underfoot and Frederic Amat's near-three-metre ceramic fountain, Font de Garotes, in the courtyard. Casa Heras serves breakfast, lunch and dinner, bookable by non-residents via the restaurant's online module; Gipsy and El Terrat hours unpublished — call ahead

coffee-gardens:Casa Cacao — Bar Cacao &.name: Casa Cacao — Bar Cacao & the obrador
coffee-gardens:Casa Cacao — Bar Cacao &.hook: Plaça de Catalunya, 23 (Bar Cacao at no. 21)
coffee-gardens:Casa Cacao — Bar Cacao &.text: Sandra Tarruella Interioristas (project lead Olga Pajares), with Callís Marès arquitectes, converted the 1960s La Esperanza clinic into Jordi Roca's chocolate house in 2020 — a contemporary reading of the confectioners' shops of the building's own era, in a palette drawn from cacao beans as they mature, mustard through brown to beige with cacao-leaf green and Girona stone grey, the bean-to-bar obrador glazed at street level. Bar Cacao daily 9:00–21:00; rooftop brunch Tue–Sun sitting at 12:45, second sitting 15:00 Fri–Sun (reservation required)

coffee-gardens:La Fàbrica.name: La Fàbrica
coffee-gardens:La Fàbrica.hook: Barri Vell (Carrer de la Llebre, 3) LAPTOP-FRIENDLY
coffee-gardens:La Fàbrica.text: A hundred-year-old carpenter's workshop down a Barri Vell alley, converted in March 2015 by Christian and Amber Meier — he rode the Tour de France before he roasted — exposed brick and copper, old timber and concrete floors under high ceilings, plus finds carried home from Bali and Japan. Daily 9:00–17:00 (venue site, 2026; closed only 25 Dec and 6 Jan); the March 2026 remote-work guide lists 8:00–17:30 — check before an early start

coffee-gardens:Espresso Mafia.name: Espresso Mafia
coffee-gardens:Espresso Mafia.hook: Barri Vell (Carrer de la Cort Reial, 5)
coffee-gardens:Espresso Mafia.text: The Meiers' 2016 second act — opened while Christian was still racing — under the medieval arcades of Cort Reial: a clinically white, laboratory-spare room arranged around the roasting operation and a custom two-group Sanremo Café Racer; the design here is the absence of everything except coffee. 9:00–20:00 per the March 2026 local guide; day-of-week detail unpublished — confirm with the venue

coffee-gardens:Cafè Le Bistrot.name: Cafè Le Bistrot
coffee-gardens:Cafè Le Bistrot.text: Unchanged in spirit since the late 1970s: a Parisian-brasserie interior at the foot of the Pujada de Sant Domènec, the terrace stacked table-by-table up the stone steps opposite the Agullana Palace — here the design pedigree is Girona's own fabric. Daily 13:00 to around midnight (2026 listings); Time Out files it under 'open until late' — kitchen hours narrower than door hours, check ahead

coffee-gardens:Idle Hands.name: Idle Hands
coffee-gardens:Idle Hands.text: Ayla Kellens — a jewellery designer by training — shaped the interior herself and hangs her own Costa Brava canvases, for sale, in this small square-side room opened at the end of 2022 with partner Jacob, a decade-deep coffee professional who ran his own roastery in Antwerp and now roasts under his Ambient label; café, natural-wine bar, record shop and gallery sharing one space. Mon 9:00–15:00; Tue–Fri 9:00–15:30; Sat 10:00–15:30; Fri–Sat also 19:00–late; Sun closed (venue site, 2026)

work:La Fàbrica.name: La Fàbrica
work:La Fàbrica.text: Girona's first third-wave café, run by a former pro cyclist — the clubhouse of the city's riding scene, open daily 9:00–17:00 when much of the Barri Vell is shut.

work:Casa Cacao terrace.name: Casa Cacao terrace
work:Casa Cacao terrace.text: A morning coffee and a chocolate on the Roca family's terrace over the river — the best-placed table in the new town for watching the coloured houses wake up.

work:Cafès on the Rambla de la Llibertat.name: Cafès on the Rambla de la Llibertat
work:Cafès on the Rambla de la Llibertat.text: The arcaded 19th-century promenade on the Barri Vell bank — a run of terraces under the vaults where the city reads its paper and takes its vermut before lunch.

work:Jardins dels Alemanys.name: Jardins dels Alemanys
work:Jardins dels Alemanys.text: A terraced garden among the ruined 16th-century barracks at the top of the walls — shade, cats, and the Cathedral's apse at eye level. Bring the book, not the laptop.

work:Parc de la Devesa benches.name: Parc de la Devesa benches
work:Parc de la Devesa benches.text: Under the tallest plane trees in Catalonia the temperature drops several degrees; the gravel avenues are where locals sit out the worst of the afternoon heat.

culture:Girona Cathedral (Santa Maria).name: Girona Cathedral (Santa Maria)
culture:Girona Cathedral (Santa Maria).hook: The widest doubt in Gothic engineering, resolved in stone.
culture:Girona Cathedral (Santa Maria).text: A single Gothic nave 22.98 m wide, 35 m high — the widest Gothic nave in the world, second among all church naves only to St Peter's in Rome. The exterior staircase is 90 steps, Baroque, built 1607. In Game of Thrones (filmed here September 2015) Jaime Lannister rides his horse up those steps to the Great Sept of Baelor.

culture:Museu d'Història dels Jueus (Cal.name: Museu d'Història dels Jueus (Call)
culture:Museu d'Història dels Jueus (Cal.hook: Eleven rooms of a medieval Jewish world, on its own ground.
culture:Museu d'Història dels Jueus (Cal.text: In the Centre Bonastruc ça Porta on Carrer de la Força, at the heart of the Call. Eleven rooms trace the daily life, learning and expulsion of Girona's Jewish community — the first Kabbalah school in Spain, founded around Nachmanides in the 13th century. Excavations here reached the medieval yeshiva.

culture:Basílica de Sant Feliu.name: Basílica de Sant Feliu
culture:Basílica de Sant Feliu.hook: The pre-cathedral church with eight Roman tombs in its walls.
culture:Basílica de Sant Feliu.text: Girona's principal church before the Cathedral, over the martyr St Felix (d. 304). A Romanesque core under a Gothic nave and Baroque façade, raised to minor basilica by Benedict XVI in 2011. Set into the presbytery are eight 3rd–4th-c. Roman and early-Christian sarcophagi, a run unique on the Iberian Peninsula.

culture:Banys Àrabs.name: Banys Àrabs
culture:Banys Àrabs.hook: 'Arab baths' that are actually 12th-century Christian Romanesque.
culture:Banys Àrabs.text: Despite the name, a Romanesque bathhouse of about 1194 modelled on Roman and Islamic precedents, not built by Muslim hands. The domed, columned central pool room (apodyterium) is the photograph everyone takes. A rare civil building of its age.

culture:Sant Pere de Galligants.name: Sant Pere de Galligants
culture:Sant Pere de Galligants.hook: A Romanesque monastery that is now Catalonia's archaeology museum in Girona.
culture:Sant Pere de Galligants.text: First documented 988, the present Benedictine church built in the first half of the 12th century, with a Lombard-banded octagonal tower. Since 1857 a museum; today the Girona seat of the Museu d'Arqueologia de Catalunya, holding the 4th-c. Sepulcre de les Estacions from Empúries. Its cloister played Oldtown's Citadel in Game of Thrones.

culture:Cases de l'Onyar & the Eiffel br.name: Cases de l'Onyar & the Eiffel bridge
culture:Cases de l'Onyar & the Eiffel br.hook: The reflected houses and the iron bridge that frames them.
culture:Cases de l'Onyar & the Eiffel br.text: The ochre-to-rust river façades are the city's signature; their palette was fixed by a 1980s restoration led by the painter Enric Ansesa. The Pont de les Peixateries Velles that crosses between them was built in 1877 by Gustave Eiffel's company — two years before he built Girona nothing else, and two decades before Paris got its tower. The personal-design credit is disputed; the firm and the year are documented.

culture:Casa Masó.name: Casa Masó
culture:Casa Masó.hook: The only Onyar riverfront house you can walk into.
culture:Casa Masó.text: Birthplace of the Noucentista architect Rafael Masó (1880–1935) and the single riverside house open to visitors — four dwellings merged, the façade reworked by Masó between 1911 and 1919. Guided tours only, small groups, booking required; city-owned since 2006 and run by the Fundació Rafael Masó.

culture:Passeig de la Muralla.name: Passeig de la Muralla
culture:Passeig de la Muralla.hook: The wall-top circuit — the city's high edge.
culture:Passeig de la Muralla.text: A walkable rampart on one of Europe's longest Carolingian wall circuits (9th–10th c.), laid over Roman fortifications because Girona guarded the frontier. Free, open dawn to night; the towers are the best free viewpoint over the Cathedral, the Barri Vell roofs and the plain of the Ter.

crafts:Ceramics — La Bisbal d'Empordà.name: Ceramics — La Bisbal d'Empordà
crafts:Ceramics — La Bisbal d'Empordà.hook: Catalonia's pottery capital, where you can still take the wheel from a named master.
crafts:Ceramics — La Bisbal d'Empordà.text: La Bisbal has thrown terracotta since the Middle Ages — the clay is in the ground and the town is built on it, with a working Terracotta museum and a live ceramicists' association. The Escola de Ceràmica de la Bisbal (founded ~1972) teaches on real kilns; its summer courses run weekly from late June to early September under named masters — Dolors Ros on wheel technique, Anna Martínez on the introduction to throwing, María Torné on porcelain — at around EUR 170 a course, booked online and open to anyone. Independent ateliers in town and nearby Peratallada run shorter bookable wheel sessions too.

crafts:Ratafia — Santa Coloma de Farners.name: Ratafia — Santa Coloma de Farners
crafts:Ratafia — Santa Coloma de Farners.hook: Macerate green walnuts into the Empordà's herb liqueur, with the cooperative that revived it.
crafts:Ratafia — Santa Coloma de Farners.text: Ratafia — the EU-protected green-walnut-and-herb liqueur — has its cultural capital at Santa Coloma de Farners, and since 2021 its first dedicated obrador: La Sobirana, a young cooperative (Ernest Morell, Pau Pujol, Pau Torra) working from an 1842 tavern-keeper's recipe. Their taller d'elaboració de ratafia is a public, bookable three-hour workshop, about EUR 50 a head — the green walnuts, herbs and alcohol for two litres included — and you leave with your own maceration to age.

quartiers:Barri Vell.name: Barri Vell
quartiers:Barri Vell.text: The old town: Roman-medieval core, stone stairs, the Cathedral and the walls.

quartiers:El Call.name: El Call
quartiers:El Call.text: The medieval Jewish quarter within the Barri Vell, folded off Carrer de la Força.

quartiers:Mercadal.name: Mercadal
quartiers:Mercadal.text: The medieval 'new town' across the Onyar — market, Devesa park, pedestrian shopping.

quartiers:Sant Pere de Galligants.name: Sant Pere de Galligants
quartiers:Sant Pere de Galligants.text: The riverside district around the Romanesque monastery, at the Barri Vell's north edge.

quartiers:Sant Feliu.name: Sant Feliu
quartiers:Sant Feliu.text: The steep lanes below the cathedral hill, around the basilica.

quartiers:Onyar riverfront.name: Onyar riverfront
quartiers:Onyar riverfront.text: The strip of coloured cases de l'Onyar along both banks between old town and new.

quartiers:Pedret.name: Pedret
quartiers:Pedret.text: The northern gateway where the Onyar meets the Ter — El Celler de Can Roca's edge of town.

quartiers:Devesa / Parc.name: Devesa / Parc
quartiers:Devesa / Parc.text: The west bank around Catalonia's largest urban park, the Fires fairground each autumn.

quartiers:Montjuïc de Girona.name: Montjuïc de Girona
quartiers:Montjuïc de Girona.text: The wooded hill over the city, historic high ground, path to the Castell de Sant Miquel.

quartiers:Vall de Sant Daniel.name: Vall de Sant Daniel
quartiers:Vall de Sant Daniel.text: The green valley of springs behind Montjuïc, up to the Romanesque monastery.

quartiers:Santa Eugènia.name: Santa Eugènia
quartiers:Santa Eugènia.text: The western district, an independent town until it was annexed in 1963.

gastronomy:Mercat del Lleó.name: Mercat del Lleó
gastronomy:Mercat del Lleó.hook: ~60 stalls: 9 fish, 11 butchers/charcuterie, fruit & veg, plus the outer ring of pagès farm stalls · esmorzar de forquilla territory by 9am
gastronomy:Mercat del Lleó.text: The working municipal market, in a 1944 hall of ~1,712 m². Mon–Fri 07:00–14:00, Sat to 14:30, closed Sun. A locals' market — go early, the fish counters thin out by mid-morning.

gastronomy:Mercat de la Devesa.name: Mercat de la Devesa
gastronomy:Mercat de la Devesa.hook: Produce, dried fruit, cured meats — plus clothes and household goods
details: Passeig de la Devesa / Ribes del Ter
gastronomy:Mercat de la Devesa.text: Girona's big open-air street market, run with the merchant guilds; the pitch shifts seasonally between the Devesa park and the Ter riverbank, so check before you go.

gastronomy:Organic producers' market.name: Organic producers' market
gastronomy:Organic producers' market.hook: CCPAE-certified fruit, veg, eggs, sheep's-milk dairy, oil, cheese
gastronomy:Organic producers' market.text: A certification-gated farmers' market — vendors must carry the Catalan organic seal — the closest thing to a true direct-from-producer market in the city. Verify the day locally; it is a small, growing stand.

gastronomy:DO Empordà cellars.name: DO Empordà cellars
gastronomy:DO Empordà cellars.text: The Alt/Baix Empordà DO, founded 1975, ~1,768 ha of low bush vines held down by the tramuntana. Visit Espelt (Vilajuïga), La Vinyeta (Mollet de Peralada), Masia Serra (Cantallops) or Terra Remota (Sant Climent Sescebes) — most take booked tastings.

gastronomy:Fesols de Santa Pau (DOP).name: Fesols de Santa Pau (DOP)
gastronomy:Fesols de Santa Pau (DOP).text: Small beans of the Tavella Brisa, Setsetmanera and Gra Petit varieties, grown only on the volcanic soils of Santa Pau and six Garrotxa villages — EU-protected (Reg. 2015/1312). The reason a plate of botifarra amb seques tastes of the Garrotxa and not just of beans.

gastronomy:Poma de Girona (IGP).name: Poma de Girona (IGP)
gastronomy:Poma de Girona (IGP).text: Five varieties (Golden, Gala, Granny Smith, Fuji among them) grown on the Gironès–Empordà plain, PGI-protected since 2003 (Reg. 1491/2003). The Ter's water and cold nights give a firm, high-acid apple — the everyday fruit of the province.

gastronomy:Formatge Garrotxa (IGP).name: Formatge Garrotxa (IGP)
gastronomy:Formatge Garrotxa (IGP).text: A grey-moulded goat's cheese from the Garrotxa, matured at least 21 days — EU-registered as a PGI only in December 2023 (Reg. 2023/2872), so recent. Nutty, faintly mushroomy from the rind; the backbone of any Girona cheese board.

gastronomy:Anxova de l'Escala.name: Anxova de l'Escala
gastronomy:Anxova de l'Escala.text: Hand-salted, wood-barrel-matured 10–12 months by houses like Solés (1888) and Callol Serrats down the coast at L'Escala. Deep local identity but no EU protection — a 'Producte de la Terra', bought straight from the factories.

gastronomy:Gamba de Palamós.name: Gamba de Palamós
gastronomy:Gamba de Palamós.text: Aristeus antennatus, landed and auctioned twice daily at the Confraria de Pescadors de Palamós under a guarantee mark that checks ground, texture and count. Seared seconds a side; a guarantee mark, not a PDO.

gastronomy:Cal Formatger.name: Cal Formatger
gastronomy:Cal Formatger.text: A Cort Reial cheese room built on Girona-province makers, Garrotxa goat's cheese to the fore, with boards to eat in and a glass of Empordà. Opens 10:30; closed Sun/Mon.

gastronomy:Casa Cacao boutique.name: Casa Cacao boutique
gastronomy:Casa Cacao boutique.text: Jordi Roca's chocolate house on Plaça Catalunya — single-origin bars and the Celler's dessert grammar to take away, over the Onyar.

gastronomy:L'Escala anchovy houses.name: L'Escala anchovy houses
gastronomy:L'Escala anchovy houses.text: An hour east, the Solés and Callol Serrats factories sell their salt-cured anchovies direct — the province's best edible souvenir, bought by weight from the barrel.

bars:DO Empordà reds.name: DO Empordà reds
bars:DO Empordà reds.hook: Garnatxa and carinyena grown on slate and tramuntana wind, in Spain's north-easternmost DO.
bars:DO Empordà reds.text: The DO was founded by Spanish order of 19 May 1975 (originally 'Empordà–Costa Brava'; the coast name was dropped and the zone widened into the Baix Empordà in 2006). Black grapes run to carinyena negra, garnatxa negra — locally lledoner — plus cabernet, merlot, syrah and ull de llebre; garnatxa alone covers roughly a third of the DO's ~1,768 ha. The wind keeps the vines low and the yields small.

bars:Garnatxa de l'Empordà.name: Garnatxa de l'Empordà
bars:Garnatxa de l'Empordà.hook: The sun-dried sweet garnatxa you drink after dinner — a protected style, not a separate DO.
bars:Garnatxa de l'Empordà.text: A traditional style inside the DO Empordà regulation, at least ~90% garnatxa. Technique: grapes are left to over-ripen and dry (the raïm assolellat / sun-dried method), harvested late — traditionally the third week of September — to concentrate sugar to around 14–15% potential alcohol before the ferment is arrested. Warm, raisined, generous. The Espolla cooperative is the classic source.

bars:Ratafia catalana.name: Ratafia catalana
bars:Ratafia catalana.hook: Green-walnut-and-herb liqueur — an EU-protected spirit GI, with its festival at Santa Coloma de Farners.
bars:Ratafia catalana.text: Registered as a geographical indication under Regulation (EC) 110/2008. The spec: a hydroalcoholic maceration of green walnuts (min. 10 g/l) for at least three months with aromatic herbs, 24–30% ABV, aged a minimum three months in wood. Home practice picks the walnuts green in June–July and macerates them in the sun for about forty days. Santa Coloma de Farners, in Girona province, is its cultural capital — the Festa de la Ratafia ran its 44th edition in 2025.

bars:Cremat.name: Cremat
bars:Cremat.hook: Rum set alight with coffee, cinnamon and lemon — the drink of the havanera nights.
bars:Cremat.text: A flambéed mix of rum, sugar, cinnamon stick, lemon peel and coffee, burned off before serving; the Cuban rum and the havanera songs both came home with sailors from the Antilles trade. Technique: it is stirred in its own flames for several minutes before being doused with coffee. Calella de Palafrugell's Cantada d'Havaneres, the first Saturday of July, is where it is drunk communally and hot.

bars:Oli de l'Empordà.name: Oli de l'Empordà
bars:Oli de l'Empordà.hook: A PDO oil pressed mainly from the local Argudell olive — the plain's other liquid.
bars:Oli de l'Empordà.text: Protected as a PDO by EU Implementing Regulation 2015/385. The zone covers the Alt and Baix Empordà with parts of the Pla de l'Estany and the Gironès; the oil is at least 51% Argudell, with Curivell, Llei de Cadaqués and Arbequina alongside. Green, faintly bitter, cut for pa amb tomàquet and for finishing suquet.

bars:Vi novell.name: Vi novell
bars:Vi novell.hook: The season's first wine, tapped around Sant Martí on 11 November.
bars:Vi novell.text: 'Per Sant Martí, mata el porc i enceta el vi' — for Saint Martin, kill the pig and broach the wine. Technique: a few weeks of aging, no more, bottled to keep the fruit and a faint natural spritz from the ferment. Drunk young and festively in the weeks after the November release; the Espolla cooperative bottles a well-known one within the DO Empordà.

bars:Vermut de l'Empordà.name: Vermut de l'Empordà
bars:Vermut de l'Empordà.hook: An Empordà vermouth built on the native garnatxa roja, not the Reus tradition.
bars:Vermut de l'Empordà.text: Celler Gerisena in Garriguella makes 'Obreboques', a vermouth on garnatxa roja — a native Empordà variety — aged two years in oak, framed by its makers as an Empordà terroir drink rather than a copy of the Reus/Barcelona style. The Sunday-noon vermut before lunch is the ritual it belongs to.

music:'La Santa Espina' — Enric Morera.name: 'La Santa Espina' — Enric Morera
music:'La Santa Espina' — Enric Morera.hook: The sardana that became a banned anthem.
music:'La Santa Espina' — Enric Morera.text: Composed by Enric Morera to a text by Àngel Guimerà, premiered 1907; the most emblematic Catalan sardana, banned under both the Primo de Rivera and Franco dictatorships. If a cobla strikes it up in Plaça de la Independència, the older dancers will rise first.

music:'El meu avi' — the havanera.name: 'El meu avi' — the havanera
music:'El meu avi' — the havanera.hook: The 1968 song that ends every Costa Brava night.
music:'El meu avi' — the havanera.text: Written in 1968 and the best-known havanera, it has closed the Cantada d'Havaneres de Calella de Palafrugell every year since 1977 — sung over a cremat, the whole square joining the last verse about a grandfather's boat lost off Cuba.

music:Cobla La Principal de la Bisbal.name: Cobla La Principal de la Bisbal
music:Cobla La Principal de la Bisbal.text: An active cobla from La Bisbal d'Empordà, in Girona province, carrying the eleven-instrument sardana tradition — the tenora's nasal reed cutting over the brass. The live soundtrack to any Girona festa where the circle-dance forms.

music:Havaneres & cremat.name: Havaneres & cremat
music:Havaneres & cremat.hook: Cuban song brought home by returning sailors.
music:Havaneres & cremat.text: The habanera crossed back to the Costa Brava with the men who worked the 19th-century Cuba trade — slow, salt-worn songs sung to guitar and accordion, always with a pot of flaming rum-and-coffee cremat going. The genre the coast made its own.

music:Nits de Clàssica in the nave.name: Nits de Clàssica in the nave
music:Nits de Clàssica in the nave.hook: Chamber music under the widest Gothic vault.
music:Nits de Clàssica in the nave.text: The city's festival puts violinists and pianists inside the Cathedral, its cloister and Sant Pere de Galligants — stone that turns a solo line vast. Hearing Bach under the 22.98 m vault is the closest thing Girona has to a house sound.
